### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-bindings.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/actions/_activation/:object/:action (route, a path literal in action))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via registerAction (symbol, a method of class ActionsFacet))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-bindings.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **55** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32242196a19570415e337b27461f4ed44773b5c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b944ff610a5bd822378f0f5ae6920df7201baf64` — the merge of head `6366e96ef9e845e55954dc6a10750ce34d9a6d85` into base `c32242196a19570415e337b27461f4ed44773b5c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b944ff610a5bd822378f0f5ae6920df7201baf64 && git checkout b944ff610a5bd822378f0f5ae6920df7201baf64
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c32242196a19570415e337b27461f4ed44773b5c 6366e96ef9e845e55954dc6a10750ce34d9a6d85 && git checkout -B drift-repro c32242196a19570415e337b27461f4ed44773b5c && git merge --no-ff 6366e96ef9e845e55954dc6a10750ce34d9a6d85

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c32242196a19570415e337b27461f4ed44773b5c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c32242196a19570415e337b27461f4ed44773b5c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `90624aa3145f420a910556ae645f687a391ae73e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/packaged-base-regime.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-bindings.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts#isServedOverrideRowOf, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-artifact-lookup.ts#shippedArtifactsOf/#lookupArtifactItem, packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/code-artifact-provenance.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts#resolveActionHandlerKeys/#standaloneActionOwnerKey, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts#handleActionsRequest/#shippingPackageOf, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts#actionPermissionError/#actionAiExposureError/#actionConfirmationRefusal/#systemObjectActionExposureError/#disabledActionRefusal/#resolveRouteActionDeclaration, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts#resumeAdmissionRefusal, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts#bindAppArtifactHandlers, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts#rehydrate/#bindArtifactHandlers, packages/core/src/kernel.ts (hook registration, plugin start order), packages/core/src/hook-dispatch.ts#dispatchHookPropagating, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts (plugin composition), packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (ActionAiSchema, visible/requiresFeature/requiresMembershipReach docblocks), docs/adr/0146 D2/D9, the flow precedent packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts.

Face: `reviewFace` over the PR's committed path list returns no schema, rules or narrowing hit (`packages/spec/src/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**` untouched); the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line decides the declaration face, which alone owes `TIER_DEFAULT`. The seat raised the review to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on card #30065 Acceptance 3 (a permission boundary: what an override may change about who may run an action), and that is the tier served here. The record is independent of the dev's self-report; every reading below is from the head's tree or `origin/main`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Admit.** `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts#CONDITIONS_DELIVERED` becomes `new Set(['flow', 'action'])`; `isOpenOverrideType('action')` therefore answers true, and `judgeOverrideWrite` judges a declared action override like a flow's: pair only (`isCustomizationPairOf`), base in the closure, base ships the name (`closure.shippers`), then the new widening check, then admit. The dependent's declaration (`declared_outside_pair`) and the pair's undeclared same-name save (`undeclared_same_name`, remedy "Declare ... or rename", never a clone) keep their refusals — pinned in `protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts` and `protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts`. The same `judgeOverrideWrite` is what `os validate` (`cli/.../override-declarations.ts#findOverrideDeclarationRefusals`) and the managed install (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` ~L3688) call, so the three doors cannot drift. Correct against D2 and D9's `action` paragraph ("admitted, once its door is cut, under conditions 1–3").
2. **Condition 1, served over the code package's name.** The by-name, execution and list reads already went through `findServedOverlayRow`/`isServedOverrideRowOf` once the type was open; the one gap, the layered read's `effective`, is closed in `protocol-lock-state.ts#declinesStoredRow` by `(servesSealedOverrideRow(type) || canonicalMetaType(type) === 'action') && isServedOverrideRowOf(row, packagedArtifactOwner(...))`. `isServedOverrideRowOf` (`served-override.ts`) judges the row's own `package_id` (must be the base's pair) and body (`overrides.package === base`), so a dependent's row and an undeclared pair row stay declined. The object read's `actions` and `getSchema(obj).actions` are the registry's bare entry, kept for action (the `SEALED_ROW_SERVED_OVERRIDE_TYPES` docblock change in `protocol-package-bindings.ts` is prose only). `everyRead` in the objectql test asserts nine reads answer `[label, BASE]`, `code.label` stays `SHIPPED`, and `run.requiredPermissions` on the schema is the override's. The run doors read exactly that: `action-execution.ts#resolveRouteActionDeclaration` reads `ql.getSchema(objectName).actions` first (rung 1), then the protocol's by-name execution read. Correct.
3. **Condition 2, rebound in one reload / restore.** `isPairRowRemoval` already keys on `isOpenOverrideType`, so the pair's delete is admitted and every read falls back to the artifact (test "condition 2"). The handler half: `engine-actions.ts#ActionsFacet.registerActionOverride` sets `{handler, package, beneath}` where `beneath` is the current entry (or the current entry's own `beneath` when re-binding the same package), and `removeActionsByPackage` walks each key's stack and drops only the named package's frames, so removing `metadata-service` re-exposes the base's `app:<id>` frame without re-registering it. `plugin.ts#resyncAuthoredActionsNow` lets a row through the artifact-shipped filter only when `isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride(row, data)` held at read time (same `isServedOverrideRowOf`, plus `standaloneActionOwnerKey(artifact) === standaloneActionOwnerKey(action)`), tracked in a `WeakSet` keyed on the parsed object (the same object is what `byKey` holds, so the lookup is sound), and binds it with `registerActionOverride`; everything else keeps `registerAction`. The resync's teardown-then-register order (remove `metadata-service` → base frame restored → override re-bound on top) gives one step in either direction. Correct for a base bound before the resync runs — see ③-1 for the case where it is not.
4. **Condition 3, one ledger row.** `disabledActionRefusal` reads `ql.isActionEnabled(actionDef.name)` by name alone; the override keeps the name, so the switch refuses the armed override with `409 ACTION_DISABLED` at both doors (REST `handleActionsRequest` after the D4 gate; MCP `resumeAdmissionRefusal`/`run_action` in the same order). `domains/actions.ts#shippingPackageOf` credits the row through `isCodeArtifactBody(action)` → `action._packageId`; the served override carries `_packageId = BASE`, `_provenance = 'package'` (asserted in test "condition 3" together with `isActionEnabled` false after `setActionActive({ name, packageId: BASE })`, `disabledActions` listing it, and the switch surviving the restore). Correct. Note: the PR does not itself assert the 409 at a door; the consult is pre-existing and name-keyed, so no new assertion is owed by this card.
5. **Acceptance 3 — `actionOverrideWidening` / `declared_action_widens_access`.** The three keys the two run doors read to decide WHO may run are exactly the three judged: `requiredPermissions` (`actionPermissionError`, both doors), `ai.exposed` (`actionAiExposureError` and `systemObjectActionExposureError`, MCP), `ai.requiresConfirmation` (`actionConfirmationRefusal`, MCP). Absent-vs-empty: `capabilities(undefined)` and `[]` both read as no capability, so a base with no gate is never "widened", and an override that omits `requiredPermissions` against a gated base drops every base capability and is refused — matches `actionPermissionError`'s `Array.isArray(...) ? ... : []`. `ai.requiresConfirmation` uses `base === true && override !== true`, which is the door's own `!== true` reading (an author's `false` and an absent key both mean no gate), so no default-on case is missed. `ai.exposed` uses `base !== true && override === true`, matching `=== true` at the door. `visible`, `disabled`, `requiresFeature`, `requiresMembershipReach` are rendering predicates lowered into `visible` (`action.zod.ts` docblocks: "UI courtesy: the endpoint's own door stays the authority"); no runtime source file outside tests reads them — correctly excluded. The refusal rides `overrideWriteRefusalError` → `code: 'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'`, `status: 403`; asserted as `{ code, status }` in the objectql test (`toMatchObject`), the metadata-protocol test (`shape(e)` = `{code, status}`), and the install test (`res.status` 403, `error.code`, rule row); the CLI test asserts `code` and `rule` (a validate row carries no status). `publishMetaItem` re-judges a draft seeded before the gate (test), so the gate is not save-only. `baseItemOf` at the protocol door is `shippedArtifactsOf(type, name, undefined, member).find(_packageId === base)`, i.e. the registry's code artifact (`lookupArtifactItem` → `getArtifactItem`, composite entries first), not the currently served override — so a re-save is judged against the true base. Correct.
6. **`target` / handler key.** The widening gate compares gates, not handlers. A pre-existing item with the maintainer touches this area; this PR adds no new route to it, and under the gate the override's audience is never wider than the base's. ③-4.
7. **`objectName`.** `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` has no `action` row, so at the protocol door the base is matched by name alone, while `overrideWriteItemsOf` (CLI, install) uses `<objectName>:<name>`. An override may therefore move a base action to another object at the save door. The handler is then not rebound (`isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride` requires equal owner keys) and the base's gates still ride the declaration, so it widens nothing; it is a consistency gap between doors. ③-3.
8. **Text changes.** `PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME.action.routes.switchOff` now spells `:object_or_global` (a placeholder description, not a route change) to keep the declared-save sentence under the REST door's 500-character bound; the save sentence for a packaged action now names the declaration first (`sealedDeclareOrRenameTail`). Prose/message only; the pinned tests in metadata-protocol and rest are updated to the new spelling. No narrowing: every input `declared_action_widens_access` refuses was refused before under `declared_type_not_yet_available`; no previously admitted input is refused.
9. **Public face added.** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `actionOverrideWidening`, `OverrideWriteClosure.baseItemOf?`, `OverrideWriteRule` member `declared_action_widens_access`. `@objectstack/objectql`: `ObjectQL#registerActionOverride`; `removeActionsByPackage` is stack-aware (identical for entries without `beneath`); `ActionHandlerEntry` is exported from `engine-actions.ts` but not reachable from the package entry (`ObjectQL.actions` is private) — the changeset's mention of it slightly overstates the public face (prose; lane seat's call). `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection`: behaviour at their doors. All additive. `Metadata-protocol: added` is right (a new accepted metadata shape). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` — consistent with the additive exports and the newly admitted shape, and with the flow precedent (#28412 shipped `minor`). `@objectstack/rest` is touched in a test file only (`rest-meta-packaged-action-permission-refusal.test.ts`); no shipped change, no changeset owed. No moved package is missing an entry. The changeset carries both declaration lines and `Skills-docs: follow-up #30505` (open, titled for this card's docs).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Must-fix (condition 2 after a restart, marketplace-installed base).** The PR body's "Known edge" assumes a base's handlers are bound only in `AppPlugin.start`, before the `kernel:ready` resync. That holds for a code-loaded package. For a marketplace-installed base — the ADR's primary case (D1: an override replaces an item of an INSTALLED, read-only base) — the handlers are bound by `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts#rehydrate` → `#bindArtifactHandlers` → `runtime#bindAppArtifactHandlers` → `ql.registerAction(objectKey, name, handler, 'app:<id>')`, inside the install-local plugin's own `kernel:ready` hook. Hooks are pushed in registration order and dispatched sequentially (`kernel.ts` hook/trigger, `hook-dispatch.ts#dispatchHookPropagating`); `serve.ts` composes `ObjectQLPlugin` before `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`, and the install-local plugin consumes the `objectql` service, so the ObjectQL resync runs first. Scenario, read from code (not run): (a) ObjectQLPlugin's `kernel:ready` `resyncAuthoredActions` runs while the base's manifest is not yet registered, so `isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride` is false (no artifact) and `isArtifactShippedAction` is false; the override row is bound as a plain `registerAction(..., 'metadata-service')`. (b) Rehydrate registers the manifest and `registerAction(..., 'app:<base>')` replaces the whole entry (`ActionsFacet.registerAction` sets the key unconditionally; its collision warning fires). (c) Rehydrate announces no `metadata:reloaded` (only install L4948 and uninstall L3051 do). Result: every read, the console button and rung 1 of the run door serve the override's declaration, but `executeAction` runs the base's body — the two definitions disagree indefinitely, until an unrelated action/object mutation or install triggers the next resync. That contradicts D9 condition 2 ("no window in which both definitions are bound or neither is") and the changeset's own sentence ("runs in place of the base's handler after one resync (`kernel:ready`, ...)") for script-body actions of installed packages; flow/api/update-typed actions (the card's `crm_convert_lead`) are unaffected since they carry no handler. The gates are the override's (never wider than the base's) and the body is the vendor's, so it is a correctness, not an access, failure. Smallest remedies: have rehydrate announce `metadata:reloaded` after binding (as install does), or run the authored-action resync after rehydrate, or let the binder slot beneath an armed `metadata-service` override instead of replacing it. Pin with a test that binds the base after the override's resync and runs.
2. **Install-door ratchet (fails closed).** `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts#heldBy` reads the base's items through `getMetaItems({ type, packageId: base })` when the base is not in the same delivery; once an override is armed, that read serves the override under the base's envelope (`_packageId = BASE`), so a re-install of `.custom` is judged against the previous override, not the base. A v2 that relaxes a v1 tightening back to the base's gates is refused at install though the protocol door admits it. Over-refusal only; a follow-up, not a blocker.
3. **`objectName` not pinned at the protocol door** (①-7): CLI/install identities carry `<objectName>:<name>`, the protocol door matches by name. No widening; door inconsistency. Follow-up.
4. **`target` seam** (①-6): a pre-existing item with the maintainer; this PR adds no new route to it. Report only.
5. Dev `open_questions`: none. `security_findings: withheld` — consistent with ③-4 being carried privately. Dev out-of-scope finding (`registerAction` over an armed override) is the mechanism of ③-1; its reach is wider than "named producer" because of the rehydrate path.
6. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay-author note owed. Check-runs on this head were still `in_progress` (Test Core shards, Type Check · workspace, Lint · repo & tooling gates) at read time; the completed ones were `success`.

### ④ Design judgment

Against D2/D9 and ADR-0066 D4: option A (refuse widening at the write gate) is the right place for "cannot be widened without saying so" — the refusal names each widened gate, is one verdict shared by save, publish, `os validate` and install, and leaves behaviour fields replaceable whole as D2 requires. The three judged keys are the complete set of declaration keys the two dispatch doors read for authorization; the comparison semantics match the doors' own reads (absent/empty capability lists, `!== true` on confirmation, `=== true` on exposure). The protocol door compares against the code artifact, not the served row, so the gate cannot be ratcheted or bypassed by a prior override there. The read-side admission reuses the one served-override predicate the flow uses, so no second judgement of the row exists. The handler stack is a sound primitive and the resync's teardown order gives one-step rebinding whenever the base is bound before the resync. The design fails its own condition 2 only in the boot ordering of ③-1, which is the deployment the ADR is written for; that is the must-fix.

## Contract review (delta, round 1)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6366e96ef9e845e55954dc6a10750ce34d9a6d85`
Local-runs: probe — the delta changes handler-stack ORDER semantics (a later `registerAction` slotting beneath a marked override, a row judged by its own declaration when no artifact is registered), which reading alone cannot settle; one throwaway worktree at this head (`pnpm install`, `pnpm --filter "@objectstack/objectql^..." build`), then `vitest run --project local src/plugin-authored-actions.test.ts` (22/22), `src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts` (13/13), `tsc --noEmit` in objectql (clean), an ablation (slot-beneath branch of `ActionsFacet.registerAction` removed → exactly the two new boot-order tests fail, `ran:BASE BODY` / `ran:REBOUND BASE BODY` where `ran:OVERRIDE` is expected; source restored), and a reviewer probe file (P1–P5 below) on the real engine + `ObjectQLPlugin.resyncAuthoredActions`; worktree removed afterwards.
Scope: .changeset/30065-declared-action-override.md, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin-authored-actions.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts#bindAppArtifactHandlers (teardown-then-register), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts#start (`kernel:ready` hook order) / #rehydrate / #installCustomizationPair (rows only, "Nothing is registered as code or ledgered") / #announceUninstall, packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts#isServedOverrideRowOf, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts#judgeOverrideWrite (`closure.shippers`, several shippers admitted), packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts#standaloneActionOwnerKey, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (composite `<packageId>:<name>` slots, `getArtifactItem`), packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts (`registerAction`/`removeActionsByPackage` contract; `registerActionOverride` is not on the contract and the plugin probes for it), docs/adr/0146 D9 conditions 1–3 and the `action` paragraph.

Face: unchanged from round 0 — the committed path list still hits no schema, rules or narrowing path (`packages/spec/src/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**` untouched by the delta as well); the declaration face (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`) alone owes `TIER_DEFAULT`; the seat's elevation to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on card #30065 Acceptance 3 is served here as in round 0. This record judges the delta `90624aa3..6366e96e` (+85 −9 over five files; the PR total is +719 −62) and the code it touches; round 0's ①/②/④ findings stand where the delta does not touch them. Every reading is from the head's tree, `origin/main`, or the probe; none from the dev's self-report.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Remedy chosen for ③-1 (round 0).** Three pieces. (a) `ActionHandlerEntry.override?: true` is set by `ActionsFacet.registerActionOverride` and carried through `removeActionsByPackage`'s `...rest` spread, so the marker survives the removal of the handler beneath it and is dropped with the override itself (probe P3: after `removeActionsByPackage('app:<base>')` the entry is `{package: 'metadata-service', override: true, beneath: undefined}`; after `removeActionsByPackage('metadata-service')` the exposed base entry carries no `override`). (b) `ActionsFacet.registerAction`: when the current entry is marked `override` and the arriving `packageName` differs, the arriving handler becomes `beneath` (replacing any previous `beneath`) and the override stays on top; no collision warning (`debug` only). (c) `ObjectQLPlugin.isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride`: when `registry.getArtifactItem('action', name)` is absent, the row is judged by `isServedOverrideRowOf(row, action.overrides?.package)` — i.e. the row's own `package_id` must be the pair of the package its own body declares, type overridable; `overrides` absent ⇒ `basePackageId` undefined ⇒ `false`, so an undeclared row still binds as a plain `metadata-service` handler and a later base replaces it (test "before the base is registered, a pair row without the declaration, or a dependent's declaration, is no override"). Correct as read and as run.
2. **(a) Boot orders — condition 2.** Code-loaded base (`AppPlugin.start` before the `kernel:ready` resync): artifact present at resync, exact judgement against `_packageId` and owner key, `registerActionOverride` over `app:<base>`; restore = resync teardown exposes the base (test "override, restore, run again"). ### ④ Design judgment

Against D9 conditions 1–3 read for `action`: the stack with an explicit override marker is the right primitive for "rebound in one reload" when the base's handlers may arrive before OR after the override's — it makes the order irrelevant for the declared pair, and the resync's teardown-then-register keeps restore a single step in both orders. Judging the row by its own declaration when no artifact is registered is a necessary concession to the marketplace boot order, and it is exact for the pair whose base later arrives; its only imprecision (①-3) is confined to configurations the engine already refuses to make well-defined (two shippers of one key) or to stale rows the ADR explicitly leaves unjudged (`basedOn` recorded, not judged). The read side is untouched by the delta and still has one predicate (`isServedOverrideRowOf`); the write gate is untouched; the switch (condition 3) is untouched. The remedy closes round 0's must-fix without re-opening any read, write or access boundary.
